target_customer: Consumers with cracked or broken iPhones, iPads and Galaxy phones, plus technicians who buy parts and kits
problem: Broken phone screens are common and a store visit or mail-in repair is slow and inconvenient. iCracked sends a background-checked technician to the customer.
business_model: Repair fees for on-demand technician visits, DIY repair kit and parts sales, device buyback, later membership plans

founders.name: AJ Forsythe
education: Cal Poly San Luis Obispo, undergraduate while founding
founders.background_notes: Started repairing iPhones for students at $75 a fix in his dorm per TechCrunch (2013). Not listed on the YC page snapshot I read.

founders.name: Tony Martin
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC company page. Background not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly marketplace operations and dispatch software; a 20-year-old UK developer built the dispatch system found on Hacker News (TechCrunch 2013). The hard part was recruiting and vetting technicians, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Repair skills and parts are widely available and the technician network could be copied, though iCracked built volume and a brand in the niche early.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Insurer SquareTrade, owned by Allstate, acquired iCracked in February 2019.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2013) reported monthly customers up about 250% after the real-time service launched and 350 contracted technicians; a 2015 article says only about 30% of owners carry device insurance.

branding.name_origin: Founder AJ Forsythe said it began as a joke: he broke his phone so often he told friends he had downloaded the iCracked app again (Christian Science Monitor, 2015).

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful; the YC description calls it uncommonly awesome and promises smiles and a 30 minute repair.

branding.brand_signature: Uber for iPhone repair positioning and the 30 minute promise

brand_strength.rationale: Press repeatedly used the Uber-for-repair framing and the name is memorable, but no source shows merch or community; limited evidence.

outcome_analysis: iCracked grew from a Cal Poly dorm repair side business into an on-demand network, reported in 2013 with 350 technicians and rapid customer growth after a real-time dispatch launch. It was acquired by SquareTrade, an Allstate company, in February 2019, as insurers bought repair channels. The price and funding history are not public in sources I could verify, so the strength of the exit is unknown.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 500 on fetch.
